## Part A

### 1. What ShipLoop already does

**Keep `carry-forward` as the named end-of-item checkpoint.** Keep per-step reflection in `document` and correct the conflicting instruction that invites `carry-forward` to edit the spec. The owner’s proposed checkpoint already has a place in the graph. The open design question is whether a separate action would catch consequential evidence that the existing checkpoint misses. [Stage table `document` and `carry-forward`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_stage_spec.py:457) · [October 28 decision](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/decisions/2026-10-28-document-reflects-no-knowledge-stage.txt:4)

I verified the source paths below, ran read-only probes of the spec and skill checks, and recounted the eight exported Q1 results. Other experiment figures are reported from the cited journals and exports. The original model sessions, product repositories and historical test runs remain unverified by me.

**Spec.** Prelude `spec` defines the living `R-<n>` contract. `implement` can add an acceptance detail, and `document` records what the built and tested step clarified or satisfied. A done `document` result requires nonblank `knowledge` entries for all three files, including a reason when one needs no change. On the normal Git route, ShipLoop checks the document edits, reviews the changed step with its code and tests, and commits them together. Against an existing committed spec, the step gate permits marked additions inside existing active requirements. It runs at `implement` and `document` completion and at the step-review import. `carry-forward` has conflicting instructions. Its writer table lists architecture and environment, but its live duty explicitly asks it to update spec satisfaction and gaps. Its general knowledge gate checks retained IDs. In a mocked-read probe, changing the text of `R-1` while keeping its ID passed that gate and failed the step-spec gate. This establishes a gate difference. Whether a live run has changed the contract that way remains unverified. [Prelude `spec`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_stage_spec.py:258) · [`DUTIES["implement"]`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1472) · [`DUTIES["document"]` and `DUTIES["carry-forward"]`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1537) · [`_handoff_fault`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4105) · [`_commit_stage`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3361) · [`STAGE_FILES` and `CLOSES`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:73) · [`check`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:314) · [`step_spec_refusal`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:645)

**Environment.** Discovery and research record sourced facts. `test-strategy` records harnesses, suites and the ID convention. `prepare` records readiness. During the build, `test`, `document` and `carry-forward` can retain working commands, fixture lifecycle and revalidation conditions. Release and operations also update the file. `prepare` requires all three living files to be nonblank, and `release-plan` and `release-verify` require environment. Missing sections, misplaced headings and passing commands absent from `## Commands` produce notices. The check that actually executes the test commands is separate from checking the file that describes them. [Knowledge writers and closes](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:64) · [`DUTIES["carry-forward"]`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1567) · [`command_notices`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:483) · [`_test_loop_gate`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:5009)

**Architecture.** `plan` records structural decisions, `test-strategy` records checks that need a real boundary, and `step-plan`, `implement`, `document` and `carry-forward` maintain the decisions and their consequences. The knowledge gate refuses dropped `AD-<n>` IDs relative to HEAD. A textual mention is enough to retain an ID, and putting a new decision under `Superseded` produces a placement notice. Those checks establish limited structural integrity. The step review examines knowledge edits alongside the change they describe. [Architecture contents and writers](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:44) · [`check`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:340) · [`placement_notices`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:826) · [Step review focus](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:2351)

**Plan steps.** `step-plan` owns the active item’s ordered steps. It checks criteria coverage, Proof inputs, path expectations and test commands. An accepted `document` advances to the next existing step. When the active plan proves wrong, `send-back` replans it with an unchanged done prefix, retained criteria and test cases, and at least one step left to execute. At the item boundary, `carry-forward` can replace the entire *future work-item queue*. The script protects current and completed IDs and checks cited `R-` and `AD-` entries and primary-requirement coverage. Prerequisite order and whether an observation reached the right owner remain judgments. The carry-forward that exhausts the queue gets the all-items Improve review before outer system testing. [Step-plan checks](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_expectations.py:352) · [`_fix_forward_refusal` and `_frozen_case_refusal`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3008) · [`_apply_accepted`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:4377) · [`check_queue`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_primary.py:179) · [`_improve_checkpoint`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:472)

**Local skills.** `carry-forward` decides `none`, `reuse`, `update` or `create`. An update or creation calls for repeat evidence, a real trial, registration under environment’s `## Skills`, and a repository index link. The reusable-skills guide also calls for a `SHIPLOOP.md` backlink. Discovery and later step plans reopen the index. The script checks the decision and reason, then card existence, `name` and `description` frontmatter and nonempty evidence for `update` or `create`. My mocked probe passed that check with no trial or index field. ShipLoop attempts a separate commit of the skill directory and listed index files. Architecture has no required skill-registration slot. ### 2. What the studies show

- **Stage placement and replanning.** October 28 was a design decision. Option C saved one model action per step and put the reflection inside the step review. The November census found eight send-backs after a documented step in the plan then in force. Seven concerned Proof or test-command construction or known tool constraints, and the eighth needed runtime diagnosis. None clearly depended on a fact first learned in the earlier step. The Q1 replay found eight of eight accepted amendments preserved the done step and corrected the fault. I confirmed the exported scores and marked prefixes. The continuation was scripted, both cases had one done step, and the model was Terra xhigh. Q2’s forward-impact question was deferred because the cases mostly gave a second chance to catch planning faults. [October 28 decision](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/decisions/2026-10-28-document-reflects-no-knowledge-stage.txt:32) · [Replan study E2 and E5](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replan-20261112/README.md:33) · [Replay revision and results](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replay-20261113/README.md:55) · [Exported Q1 scores](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replay-20261113/q1-pilot-scores.json:1)
- **Progressive learning.** Round 5 reported that both judges found actionable forward facts in 86 of 160 sampled `learned` lines. Repeated refusals cost 0.8% of recorded time. Removing the two-commit look-back changed no hidden check and met the study’s rule for no demonstrated benefit. The live comparison kept the knowledge home, used two- or three-step items in one conversation, and ran Sol medium and Sonnet **high**. The archived census was predominantly Terra. The result gives little reason to add more within-run recording and leaves cleared-context and later-run value open. The existing end-of-work review also changed code or tests in 10% of one-step and 21% of multistep items in the earlier census. Those are edits, with their effect on outcomes unmeasured there. [SDLC Round 5 R34–R40 and Limits](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-sdlc-structure-journal.md:949) · [SDLC Round 1 R7](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-sdlc-structure-journal.md:120)
- **Closing looks and spec growth.** Ratchet’s two outside judges jointly accepted 10 of 59 additions and two of 23 reported gaps. Six of nine tested additions in one ticket run rejected a correct reference. In another run, an added clause led to rewriting 21 earlier checks. The pilot’s three-cycle apparatus ended while looks were still adding clauses. The ShipLoop candidate with a fresh worker found real issues, but the two audited deliveries showed no gain under the registered rule and took 1.4 and 2.0 times baseline. A separate experiment with a fresh look **and** an Opus xhigh fix did improve some deliveries. That combined intervention leaves the look’s independent contribution unresolved. [Ratchet pilot §10 F15 and F21](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/ratchet-pilot-journal.md:531) · [Ratchet pilot §13](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/ratchet-pilot-journal.md:749) · [Head-to-head §§15 and 20](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/ratchet-vs-shiploop-journal.md:1080) · [Integrated candidate audit](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/ratchet-vs-shiploop-journal.md:1593)
- **Knowledge across runs.** Multipass E2 measured a benefit from tighter existing writer instructions and notices. The three second passes added zero stray environment headings each, versus 7, 6 and 8 in controls. All 12 runs passed, and second-pass median time was 1.02 times control. The later four-pass chain still had stale `Planned` statements in every final architecture. The follow-on journal demonstrated that a recommendation can produce a runnable request and a later delivery on primed examples. Its audit leaves natural demand and repair value open. [Multipass E2](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-multipass-journal.md:329) · [Multipass Round 5](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-multipass-journal.md:825) · [Follow-on Round 7 F45](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-follow-on-run-journal.md:895) · [Follow-on Round 8 audit](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-follow-on-run-journal.md:942)
- **Getting knowledge used.** The platform study showed that a seeded local environment fact can change the delivered product on both target drivers. On its matched shared-page fixture, a passive pointer delivered the fact in zero of three products, while a printed block and an exact spec-stage directive each delivered it in three of three. The forty-fact comparison found no context saving from pages, and its hand audit corrected keyword scoring in both directions. These were small, intentionally seeded cases. The October planning analysis supplies a separate cost warning. It measured 22.05 planning minutes in one older Grok medium run and found repeated reading and compaction, with quality unmeasured. It supplies no timing estimate for a new stage on the target drivers. [Platform §§32–33](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/platform-knowledge-journal.md:1235) · [Platform §37](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/platform-knowledge-journal.md:1458) · [Platform §§50–53](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/platform-knowledge-journal.md:2100) · [Planning time §§1–4](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/planning-time-analysis-2026-10-06.md:14)

### 3. Recommendation for the five parts

- **Spec — change the existing carry-forward duty.** Remove its instruction to write back satisfaction and gaps directly to `spec.md`. Put observed clarifications and evidence in the guarded step reflection and review. At item close, route a newly discovered gap as an obligation or corrective item. A change in intended behavior requires an explicit scope decision. Closing synthesis can expose a real gap, as two of Ratchet’s reported gaps show. Giving that synthesis another chance to author requirements risks turning an implementation choice into a contract that rejects correct products. [Step-spec gate](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:645) · [Live carry-forward duty](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1567) · [Ratchet pilot §§10 and 13](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/ratchet-pilot-journal.md:749)
- **Environment — leave the stages as they are.** Keep the concrete command, fixture dependency or platform fact where the next planner will find it, with scope and a revalidation condition. That can change a real delivery. Adding an item-by-item report risks burying the fact and repeating the growth that the multipass change reduced. [Carry-forward knowledge duty](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1567) · [Multipass E2](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-multipass-journal.md:353) · [Platform §33](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/platform-knowledge-journal.md:1268)
- **Architecture — leave the stages as they are.** Update the decision or boundary whose operation changed. If a skill is how that decision is implemented or revalidated, link its card from that `AD-<n>` or real-boundary check. That gives the link a specific reader and purpose. Followed `AD-` entries can be quoted in the consuming packet. A mandatory architecture entry for every skill would duplicate the existing registry and could leave a stale link with no consumer. [Architecture contents](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py:44) · [`_followed_lines`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:7112) · [Reusable skill registration](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py:1625)
- **Plan steps — leave the routing as it is.** Fix the unfinished suffix through the existing send-back when new evidence changes the active plan. At item close, update a pending item’s `context` or add corrective work when there is a specific consumer and consequence. A focused checkpoint might catch a dependency the producer overlooked. Routine replanning can unsettle accepted proofs or drop independent work from a replacement queue. The historical late cases support better initial Proof selection and fix-forward more directly than another pass. [Fix-forward gate](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py:3008) · [Carry-forward queue contract](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/references/carry-forward.md:67) · [Replan study E2 and E5](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replan-20261112/README.md:33)
- **Local skills — leave the conditional duty at carry-forward.** A genuinely recurring procedure can repay the effort if a fresh reader finds it and succeeds on a later task. The recorded `none` decisions give little evidence for eliciting more skills routinely and say little about missed opportunities on other work. Use the existing cold-reader trial when a concrete opportunity appears. An index link and frontmatter establish discoverability only on paper. [SDLC Round 5 F29](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-sdlc-structure-journal.md:1052) · [Reusable product skills, cold-context trial](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/references/testing-and-documentation.md:802)

### 4. The cheapest test that would change my recommendation

**Replay one real item boundary where new evidence from W1 changes a W2 already in the queue.** Freeze the checkout and accepted evidence after W1’s last reviewed commit. Use a case in which the relevant fact first became observable during W1 and the original request already authorizes the necessary W2 change. In the control, run the existing `carry-forward`. In the treatment, move its reflection duty into a separate, fresh advisory packet at that boundary, with the same facts and instructions. Feed its finding through the same `carry-forward` submission and checks. Start W2 cold in both arms. Score its delivered behavior with a hidden executable check calibrated on a correct implementation and a known wrong one, and rerun inherited checks. Verify what each model actually received. The historical replay explains why the evidence must be frozen at the boundary, and the Sol packet audit shows why printed text alone is insufficient evidence of exposure. [Replay reconstruction review](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replay-20261113/astra-review.md:78) · [Platform §47](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/platform-knowledge-journal.md:1960)

**Register the rule first.** Start with one matched Sol 6.2 medium pair. Qualify only if the control misses the designated W2 check, the treatment passes it, inherited checks stay green, approved scope and W1’s records stay intact, and the checkpoint adds at most 60 seconds before W2 starts. The 60 seconds is my proposed pilot budget. Repeat on Sonnet 5.5 medium only after a qualifying Sol result. Two qualifying pairs would change my recommendation to a **targeted advisory pilot** at consequential boundaries. A tie, regression, scope drift, excess cost or mixed result keeps the current placement. An invalid fixture or missing instruction makes the comparison inconclusive. Cost is **two to four remaining-delivery continuations, with zero reruns of W1**. This screens for a large benefit on one mechanism. A permanent duty on every item would still need evidence about how often that occasion occurs. [Replay Q1 limits](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/experiments/step-boundary-replay-20261113/README.md:158) · [Follow-on Round 8 audit](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/docs/shiploop-follow-on-run-journal.md:946)

## One thing the owner should hear

An open item due at `carry-forward` is treated as settled when that work item’s later `carry-forward` returns done. The settlement code checks the stage and ordering. It does not require evidence that the finding was resolved or mapped to a queue item. If a consequential obligation disappears between items, trace that transition first. It is a concrete failure mode to measure before adding another reflection stage. [`open_items` and `_settled`](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_assumptions.py:187) · [Carry-forward contract](/private/tmp/review-wa2VxT/skills/shiploop/references/carry-forward.md:109)
